claims.text: Funding is available for tuition fees for undergraduate students.
The funding is for students at Scottish higher education institutions.
The funding is for students from low-income households.
The funding is for students who are ineligible for government tuition fee support.
Applications are processed on a first-come-first-served basis.
The grant covers the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain under a visa valid for the entire duration of the course, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g. grants or loans) towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, unless seeking support for a second undergraduate degree under specific conditions.
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of the loans available.

CEF will not consider an application if you are eligible for support (including loans) from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
In general, CEF will not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications from students who previously received funding from the Carnegie Education Fund for an undergraduate degree and wish to start a different course may not be considered.
Part-time students in receipt of tuition fee support from SAAS may apply if the amount awarded by SAAS is less than the total amount of fees payable.
Students who came to Scotland to study at university or college but have no experience of education in Scotland before that, and no other ties to Scotland, will not be considered eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree level qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of CEF.

Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, a full-time, part-time or distance learning undergraduate degree course in academic year 2026-27 at a Scottish institution or a course validated by a Scottish university but delivered in Scotland.

HNC and HND diploma courses, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with a graduate entry, courses outside Scotland, courses at a Scottish HEI delivered and validated by a university outside Scotland, Open University courses, CPD courses, and university courses below degree level are not eligible for support.

The Carnegie Education Fund has a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start an undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have been unable to gain employment in the subject area of their previous degree, be unemployed, have been made redundant or be facing redundancy.

Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must wish to reskill in a different field of study, unrelated to their previous qualifications and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
The median household income of award-holders in 2025-26 was £10,000 per year.
All applications are made online.

Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student can demonstrate that they were first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after CEF’s online portal has closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their applications within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and references are submitted promptly.
Supporting documents can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
